reviews.text: Wow i Dont Leave Reviews unless a Game really impresses me... So this would be my 3rd review ever in my 13 years + on steam. This game Scratch's my itch for destruction of a City/empire, Love the after action reports of the dead and destruction of buidlings. its very addicting and has elements of depth with the ability's and upgrades, i only wish levels were bigger! like hundreds of npcs haha The best part is seeing your Bloody Rampage aftermath, all the dead around just makes you feel like a Powerfull Mf. hoping to see more of this or see it updated because this games a true gem and is really really under looked we need more games like this fresh breath of air. Edit: Upon putting 50+ hours into this game i can say confidently it is one of my all time top 3 games i can always play and never get bored with, so let me give you a better perspective of this treasure that many will miss out on... upon 1st glance you probably think the graphics aint good - or the game is cheap so it cant be good? or even he fact its just early access may even deter you from experiencing this little gem! Well let me explain and mabe you might give this fresh breath of air in this current gaming industry of stagnant half finished disappointing games. - Break the Empire Starts you out lettin you choose your Evil Villain -1st: is the Evil Cult Leader who Can Brain wash The Local Unwashed Rabble to Fight (and Die) for his Beck and Call... Turn the local villagers against eachother and enjoy the slaughter or even get your hands dirty and join the fun! throw your daggers at them if you dont want your brainwashed servants to do your bidding!!! its highly enjoyable seeing an army of people bent to your will Marching on your orders destroying the very villages/citys they helped create while dieing from there own friends and protectors Hands!!! Remember your in control so dont feel remorse and savor the battlefield after each battle its always littered with the dead and Rubble of destroyed buidlings. After all you are The Cult Leader So dont forget to spend that "you" time relishing your carnage! -2nd: is The Old Hag aka Necromancer another very fun but also very different character! start as an Ugly Hag who smell like a Corpse herself the stench akin to rotten meat, on the outskirts of a tiny village she Comes upon her 1st unlucky soul picking some flowers, frolicking thru the ferns until they smell something Dead and look around until they see this old lady with a grin that gives them chills shes in rags mabe its someones grandmother who needs help? mabe shes just a crazy old bat who needs help finding her way back to town?? then they see her Cast a spell which unbeknownst to them it raises the corpse of the bandits they killed and buried in the shallow grave behind them last harvest, then more corpses start rising all around the dead of the past buried all over the land start to rise and they Feast and gorge on the living!!! with the witch she loves her poison use her spells to kill and taint the citizens of the empire with her powerful hand crafted poison, have your undead army wreak havoc on the citys and soldiers of the soon to be dieing empire!! -3rd: Burnie the happy go Lucky Demon (became one of my favorites) in this Play-thru take Charge of an Entity older than the Empire itself Born in the infernal Fires of the the underworld finally granted your time in Reality above in the realm of Man, your the definition of Evil, Watch the Empire burn! the Flames are your friend! create a small fire on the forests edge and watch it Consume the land in a roaring Blaze of unstoppable Chaos consuming the land via grass, trees, logs flowers, ferns and eventually the wooden dwellings that the Weakling Mortals call "homes" burn it all then Collect the Ashes of the fires as Sustenance for your growing power! did i mention your also demonically fast? those pesky mages wont ever catch you with there Laughably slow spells make them pay for there insolence and burn them to cinders! the king can hide behind behind his serfs and nobles but Burnie always Pays the Devils Due!!! -4th- The ice Witch is another option to try, Do you Hate Global Warming?? ever wanted to start a 2nd ice age? are you sick of the Greenery and ate hate summer fall and spring? then ice Lady is your Go to! freeze the Feeble Weak unwashed peasants to Death! Kill the Crops that feed them! with your Frost make every step you take turn to ice, seeing the frozen corpses of the peons you slay with your ice magic always brings me joy, shes unique (aint soar on the eyes either if you catch my drift) but watch out shes ice cold and may shatter your heart into a million frozen ice shards! -5th- Ever wanted to get Stoned? Well then this game got you! [Enter] Stone Lady! Ugly as Sin with a face only a mother could love abnormally tall and uber slow But Deadlier than all the Above this Powerhouse of a She-man Can kick some Major Empire A*s she willl use her Stone Magic to Break the bones and Armour of the bravest knight, she can cast the grandest structures of the Toughest Material made by the Kings finest Architects to Rubble! she may look like a Troll but i assure you she can really mess a Kings day up real quick with her ability to Kick a*s!!! now that the characters have been listed i will bring up game mechanics, as i said above n burnies the fire aspect is really neat and very satisfying to see a fire you made or even an enemy archer make with a flaming arrow Spread and get out of hand itts something ive never really seen in a game like this on that type of scale before, wicked cool seeing the building and people burnt to crisp after an accidental fire made by the enemy themselves lol, the there is the rings and necklaces of power each grants really cool perks, longer range, more damage on a spell, make a spell cost less mana (the good Ol Blue stuff baby) to cast. mabe a ring will make your spell cast 2-3-5 projectiles at once! but watch out your spells can backfire and kill you lol so be mindful! there is variety in the magical items as well ranging from poor, common, uncommon, rare, and epic which depending on its status makes your magical item more powerful, you keep your items you find after each run, and the items usually drop from a Special Named enemy (which is another awesome aspect the named enemy's are heroes and mini bosses who can really mess your day up but when killed give more exp and drop either item or a skill upgrade) then once your back after a run if you dont like the magic items you have then just cast them into the forge and melt them down to create a new one of random origin ad depending on what you use makes it stronger! the variety of enemies is satisfying and the Game dev has been adding more enemy's and maps he tends to his loyal fans (something alot of devs don't do) its a 1 man show and honestly blows my mind because i love video games and ill buy these 40$ and 60$ triple A games and just be so let down especially with alot of newer games coming out but with this it just captured me and renewed my faith in the game industry and for the price its just a no brainier on this one... sure mabe the game aint for some but if you wanna play for an hour or 5 this games the type you can jump in and out of on a drop of a dime! the Dead Bodys Stay (love that in any game) you can Destroy entire citys, murder a Forest full of Magical Folk like fairy's mushroom People, kill an Ancient you sentient Tree ( its a weir-wood like in game of thrones) Slaughter Drunken Dwarf Miners in there Mountain Hole where the Toil banging on Rocks while incoherently Mumbling some type of dwarven swear words at eachother! all in all 9/10 (no such thing as a 10/10) for me its now one of my favorites which ill be playing often for the rest of my adult life until a squeal or similar game comes along but the best part is the games not even Finished and it already that enjoyable! he still cookin !!

Looked fun at first, but there are severe balancing issues and the ending basically kicked me in the teeth. Severe Balancing Issues: Lots of cool abilities and characters, many of the abilities have a toggle for auto aim and such, but the way that it is currently running you never have enough mana to always have even half of your abilities on. Essentially you're always in a severe mana deficit. In addition, the leveling makes it so that you usually gain a flat damage to a spell/ability but the mana cost increases as well, and you're so behind in mana from the beginning game that you almost always have to devote anywhere between 10-15 of your hard earned "general" levels into mana recovery or cheaper spell cost. Counter intuitively, leveling up your active spells is often not worth it. If you level up your strongest spell, its usually a flat damage rate up (+1 for example) and your mana cost increases too (+1). You use up almost all your mana (unless you're a summon build, but that has its own challenges) so you have to sink your general skill points into mana recovery or cheaper spell. The damage increase from leveling the active spell isn't worth it, because it very easily becomes too expensive to afford to cast more than a few times. Without meta progression and decent items, its actually better to NOT level up the active skill and to increase your damage via the "damage" general skill, which provides a percentile boost. This is an issue when you are forced to invest so many of your general skills into other essential level ups: mana recovery/cheaper spell/speed/health regen/faster casting time/etc. There are builds where you can just safely and painstakingly slowly cheese every enemy. While other builds without significant meta progression is impossibly infeasible. Meta progression is in the form of legacy items and additional general skill points based off of the number of achievements you got. This hurts when I spent hours on a good run, got to the final area, and found a hell forge (reroll items). I dropped my full inventory of good loot and grabbed the trash loot to reroll them, when I got attacked by the boss and killed him. The game ends right then and there and forces you to exit to the main scene. I lost everything. Which is a punch in the gut, especially as every other area allows you to leave and move on after you have the opportunity to stay for as long as you like.
Needs a lot of work but granted it's a small team. More depth, more choices and the random maps can screw you over very quickly

Good highs, but the lows are awful. The balance is all over the place. Some characters are free wins, meanwhile others are a nightmare to play. For example, all the cult leader needs to do is successfully mind control a few elites/bosses in the first few maps and he's already won. Meanwhile, the necromancer struggles because her minions are nowhere near as beefy or strong. The terrain generation for the dwarf caves is atrocious, especially for summon builds. You have to manually destroy the terrain to build a tunnel since minions can't jump across holes. This translates to holding a directional key for a few minutes - very monotonous. Certain elites and named enemies are also very frustrating to play against. There are two in particular: one that revives dead enemies, and another that has an aoe heal. Good luck if both or multiples of them decide to spawn together. It's a great concept but it definitely needs more balancing. Wait for a few patches.

Very cool game with a lot of potential but when you hit a wall it feels so utterly miserable. There's an enemy that constantly pulses aoe healing to all nearby enemies that makes for some of the most soul crushing experiences in the game. If you don't pass a minimum dps check you are stuck and an ever growing immortal army will follow you to the ends of the earth. If you happen to be playing minions and run into this your minion will wipe and you will get stuck in a summon death loop unable to progress. Good to see the dev is listening to feedback and hopefully some of the rough edges get smoothed out over time but in its current state its a no from me.

All I can say about this game is that it's cheap and that at this price point, you'll likely play it enough to get "your moneys worth" out of it. But it's not satisfying time. It looks like it might be good. It's like one of those 90's shareware games you'd try out and you'd be like, oh, this is cool, and you'd send some guy $10 in the mail or something and he'd give you a code. That's a compliment - those games were fun. I enjoyed digging through game download sites to uncover little gems. But this game is completely unbalanced and hits you with gotchas and those games were not like that. There's like 8 different characters you can play as. The guy you play as in the demo is the best of them by far that I've seen. He's limited, but he's alright. If the other guys were like that, this would be a tentative thumbs up. But the other characters are awful. I was going to get into the specifics of those characters, but those are symptoms. The real problems of this game come from this: 1. Every skill costs too much mana and every single skill uses mana. So when you build your character, you're pretty much forced to specialize in the active skills which preserve or regen mana which takes up nearly all of your 'active skill points'. None of the other stuff except increasing spell damage (which again is about getting more mileage out of your mana) makes any difference. If you run out of mana, you're dead. This is even true at level 1, where your spells are not only pitiful, but you quickly run out of mana even fighting low quantities of the most common mobs and have to run around, trying to regen it. 2. Gaining levels isn't good, really. Because then your spells just cost more mana. You don't get a sense of "I gained a level. That's good.", in this game. It's "How do I reduce the harm caused by the new drain on my mana?" 3. Many player skills are often so weak as to be useless, drain your mana dry for too little payback, or directly work against your other skills. As an example of the last, there's a cult leader character whose main skill is charming enemies to fight for him. Well, he's got that skill as well as other skills which damage enemies. Most skills in this game are automatically fired, so you're simultaneously getting someone on your side with charm while beating the crap out of them with your damage spells. If you charm him, he's now on your side with 5 hit points. As often as not you kill him before you can do so. 4. The levels are designed in such a way.... so there are I think 5 levels in the game. You've got one character whose best skills require him to be on or around water. You've got others whose best skills require dirt, or flammable materials. One of the 5 levels is in a mine, which is almost entirely rock and has no water at all. The final boss level is in a castle which again, is all rock. What do those characters do? Their best skills become useless at the time of the game where they most need them. Through 40% of the game they can't use their core competency at all, or at least without a great deal of hassle. So nominally there's a lot of skills but there's really just one optimal way to play with each class. I can't see anyone going anywhere in this game unless they go nuts with mana regen and reducing spell mana cost and being entirely about mana management. I probably shouldn't mention this but the names are weird. Stuff like (and I'm paraphrasing)... "Buttfart Village" and so on. I feel like this could have been good. All the work was done to make it good. It's just that the decisions about balancing weren't well thought out. The names of everything kind of hint that the dev didn't take this too seriously, which fair enough but he did all the hard work... why not figure out balance and change some variables here and there and make this game three times better for minimal effort? I don't really get it. Meh... I'm investing too much time in this review. I mean, it's cheap. You'll play it enough that you're not cheated. I'll probably toy with it a bit more because the game has that 1990's fun game vibe and I want that vibe, even though logically I know this game can't give it to me. But you're best off avoiding it.
